title: fix(app-shell): read the single AI quota pool and draw one ring (objectui#8524)
body:
Fixes #8524

> ⏸️ **Parked on an external gate, not a defect of this PR:** the required `Spec Main Shape Gate` fails every objectui merge group (`report-chart-query-spec-parity.test.ts` line 747, `TS1360`, against objectstack `df3ba164a588`). Anchor card: objectstack-ai/objectui#10916. This PR is re-queued by the claiming seat when that card closes.

Clause-②: no

## What was wrong

After objectstack-ai/cloud#2144 the tenant runtime's `GET /api/v1/ai/usage` answers `{ pool, breakdown }`: one AI quota pool, plus an observation-only split of that same pool. `useAiUsage` only parsed the retired per-meter `{ meters: { build, dataChat } }` answer, so its parser returned `null` and `AiUsageIndicator` rendered nothing. No ring, no error.

Producer read at cloud `main` `96eb092`, `packages/objectos-runtime/src/ai-usage-endpoint-plugin.ts` (symbols `AiUsageIndicator`, `AiUsageBreakdownFractions`, `AiUsageResponse`, `buildAiUsageResponse`, `unknownResponse`):

- `pool` carries `planType`, `fraction` (number or null), `unmetered`, `resetKind`, `resetsAt`, `upgrade`, `topUp`. These are the same fields each old meter carried.
- At that sha `breakdown` is always an object whose members are number or null. Every error path answers 200 with a neutral pool (`fraction: null`) and both members `null`.
- Cloud ADR-0015 makes the `build` / `dataChat` split read-only statistics that no quota decision uses. cloud#2133 lets the endpoint keep `breakdown` but does not require it, so its absence is a normal reading. The triage comment on the card says the same.

## What changed

- **`useAiUsage`** reads `{ pool, breakdown? }` and only that shape.
  - `pool` must carry every declared field with its primitive type. `resetKind` and `planType` are checked as strings, so a reset kind this build does not know still renders without a reset line (the objectui#7371 behaviour, still pinned).
  - A missing `breakdown`, or one with `null` members, is a normal reading and never the parse-failure branch.
  - Any other answer, the retired `{ meters }` one included, gives `usage: null` and now also sets `error`. **There is no dual-shape read.**
- **`AiUsageIndicator`** draws ONE ring from `pool`.
  - The status, the reset line and the upgrade / top-up CTA all read the pool.
  - The split appears as text in the popover under the pool's row: a "Used so far" heading, then e.g. `Build 30%` and `Ask 20%`, each a percentage of the same pool. It is shown only when at least one member is a number, and it is never a second ring.
  - The CTA's test id is now `ai-usage-cta`.
- **i18n**: one new key, `console.ai.usage.breakdownTitle`, in every locale pack. The split rows reuse `meterBuild` / `meterAsk`.
- **Changeset**: `.changeset/8524-ai-usage-single-pool.md` declares a patch for `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n`.

File surface is the claim's: the hook, the component, their two test files, the ten locale packs and one changeset. The hooks barrel is untouched (see Acceptance notes).

## Tests

`packages/app-shell/src/hooks/__tests__/useAiUsage.test.ts`:

- the new shape parses to `{ pool, breakdown }`;
- `breakdown` absent parses to `{ pool }` with no error;
- `breakdown` with both members `null` parses as a normal reading;
- the retired `{ meters }` answer gives `usage: null` with `error` set (the strict reader, pinned);
- a `breakdown` member that is not a fraction gives `usage: null`.

`packages/app-shell/src/layout/__tests__/AiUsageIndicator.test.tsx`:

- ONE ring in the trigger even when the split is measured;
- the split is listed as text with no ring inside it, and the popover holds exactly one ring;
- both members `null` gives one ring and no split;
- `breakdown` absent gives one ring and no split;
- unmetered or null-fraction pool renders nothing;
- low hint, CTA and the weekly reset cases, ported to the pool;
- through the REAL hook: a `{ pool }` answer with no `breakdown` renders the ring, and the `{ meters }` answer renders nothing once the hook reports its error.

**Reverse verification** (after committing the fix; mutation and restore scripted with a trap): restoring the base versions of `useAiUsage.ts` and `AiUsageIndicator.tsx` under the new tests gives `Test Files 2 failed (2)`, `Tests 20 failed | 4 passed (24)`. The 4 that stay green are the shape-independent cases: null usage renders nothing, non-2xx, inert without apiBase, and refetch on nudge. The restore was proven by HEAD blob hashes and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

## Local verification

Final reading at `12e1c1d`. That head is this branch after merging `origin/main` three times; the merges brought no change to the files this PR touches. Each exit code was captured to a file before any pipe. The full app-shell suite ran once, at `fd6907c` (the fix commit): `Test Files 843 passed | 1 skipped (844)`, `Tests 8673 passed | 9 skipped`. It was not re-run at the final head, because CI runs it.

Also run at `a5d7c25`, after the first merge (which touched the locale packs): the `packages/i18n/` suite plus the two touched tests plus the two ChatDock tests gave 76 files and 1234 tests passed, exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` confirms the package type-check compiles both touched test files.

Lint was narrowed to the diff's `.ts` / `.tsx` files. The narrowing is safe because `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions` / `project` / `projectService` / type-checked preset (zero hits, with a lit control), has no `import/*` plugin rules, and none of `eslint-rules/*` reads another file. Every rule therefore judges one file, and this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. The count comes from `--format json`: 14 files, 0 errors, 2 warnings. Both warnings are `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` on effects this diff does not change, and linting the base blobs of those two files shows the same two warnings.

## Acceptance notes

- **Split placement**: in the popover, which is the indicator's detail view, rather than in a native `title` tooltip. The card allows "a tooltip or a detail view", and a `title` tooltip never shows on touch devices.
- **Strict `breakdown`, decided by the PM on the dev report (a PM decision, not a maintainer ruling: option A, keep strict)**: a `breakdown` that is present but malformed is rejected like any other unreadable answer. `error` is set and the ring hides. "Malformed" means not an object, a member that is neither a number nor null, or a literal `breakdown: null`, which the producer never sends. The alternative, dropping a malformed split and keeping the ring, would be exactly the tolerant read the card's routing constraint forbids, and it would hide a future rename on the producer side. Only an absent `breakdown`, or one with null members, means "no split".
- **`error` on an unreadable answer**: the hook now sets `error` when an answer does not parse. Before, it returned `usage: null` with no error. No UI reads `error` today.
- **Type names**: `AiMeterUsage` keeps its name and now documents the pool. The new `AiUsageBreakdown` lives in the hook file. Neither change touches `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/index.ts`, which is outside the claimed surface. The package entry `src/index.ts` re-exports none of these types, hence `Clause-②: no`.
- **Delivery order**: the cloud tenant image bundles objectui at cloud's `.objectui-sha` (the overlay layer in `apps/objectos/Dockerfile`). So this reader ships with a runtime that already serves `{ pool, breakdown }`. The one path where it could meet a `{ meters }` runtime is a hotfix branch that moves the pin without cloud#2144. That path is noted here and deliberately not answered with a dual read.
- **Out of scope**: nothing found that qualifies for a new card.
